IS : 6213 ( Part 20 ) - 1984

Indian Standard METHOD OF TEST FOR PULP
PART 20 DETERMINATION OF ALKALI RESISTANCE OF PULP

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard (Part 20) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 12 December 1984, after the draft finalized by the Paper and Its Products ( Excluding Packaging Materials ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard describes the gravimetric determination of alkali-insoluble constituents of the pulp and applies to all categories of pulps. 0.3 This standard is mainly based on IS0 699-1982 `Pulps -Determination of alkali Resistance', issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). 0.4 In reporting the results of a test or analysis, made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS: 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard (Part 20) specifies a method for the determination of the alkali-insoluble fraction of pulps using sodium hydroxide solution of fixed concentration. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 R-Value -- Alkali resistance; the insoluble fraction expressed as a percentage by mass of the oven-dry pulp. 2.2 R 18 ,R 10 ,R 5 , or Rc -- R-values in which the indices 18, 10, 5 or c refer to the chosen concentration, in grams of sodium hydroxide per 100 g of solution.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

3

IS : 6213 ( Part 20 ) - 1984 3. QUALITY OF REAGENTS 3.1 Unless otherwise specified pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1977* ), freshly boiled and cooled shall be employed in the tests.
NOTE -- `Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

4 PRINCIPLE 4.1 Defibering of the pulp under specified conditions in sodium hydroxide solution of chosen concentration. 4.2 Filtering of the insoluble fraction, washing with sodium hydroxide solution of the same concentration and temperature as that used for defibering, and acidification, washing, drying and weighing. 5. REAGENTS 5.1 Sodium Hydroxide Solution -- of known concentration, containing less than 1 g of sodium carbonate per litre ( see Notes 1 and 2 ), for example: a) --5.39 � 0.03 mol/1 solution, containing 18.0 � 0.1 g of sodium hydroxide per 100 g of solution ( Q 2 0 =1.197 2 g/ml ), equivalent to 215.5 � 1.0 g of sodium hydroxide per litre; b) -- 2.77 � 0.03 mol/l solution, containing 10.0 � 0.1 g of sodium hydroxide per 100 g of solution ( Q 20 = 1.108 9 g/ml ), equivalent to 110.9 � 1.0 g of sodium hydroxide per litre; and c) -- 1.31 � 0.03 mol/l solution, containing 5.0 � 0.1 g of sodium hydroxide per 100 g of solution ( Q 20 = 1.053 8 g/ml ), equivalent to 52.7 � 1.0 g of sodium hydroxide per litre.
NOTE 1 -- The sodium hydroxide solution may be conveniently prepared as follows: Dissolve a quantity of solid sodium hydroxide in an equal mass of water and allow the suspended sodium carbonate to settle. Decant the supernatant liquid and dilute with carbon dioxide-free water to the appropriate concentration. Check by titration with standard acid solution. NOTE 2 -- Although sodium hydroxide solution generally possesses the maximum dissolving power at a concentration of about 10 percent ( m/m ), certain pulps show maximum solubility at some lower or higher alkali concentration. If the R-value of an unknown pulp or of a new type of pulp is to be determined with the sodium hydroxide solution of maximum dissolving power for the pulp, it is necessary to establish a solubility diagram using several different concentrations in order to determine the sodium hydroxide concentration of maximum dissolving power.

5.2 Acetic Acid -- 1.7 mol/l solution, corresponding to 100 ml of CH3COOH ( Q 20 = 1.055 to 1.058 g/ml ) per litre.
*Specification for water for general laboratory use ( second revision ).

4

IS : 6213 ( Part 20 ) - 1984 6. APPARATUS 6.1 Beaker -- of capacity 250 ml, flat-bottomed, made of alkali-resistant material. 6.2 Stirring Rod -- of diameter 15 mm, with a flat end, made of a nonbrittle alkali-resistant material, preferably hard plastics. 6.3 Filtering Device -- of capacity 80 to 100 ml, internal diameter about 30 mm, with a bottom made of sintered glass of pore size ranging from 160 m to 250 m. 6.4 Weighing Bottle -- with a lid. 6.5 Constant Temperature Bath -- capable of a maintaining a temperature of 20 � 0.2�C. 7. PREPARATION OF THE TEST SAMPLE 7.1 If the pulp is in slush form, remove the water by suction taking pre cautions to avoid the loss of fine fibres, press between blotters and dry at a maximum temperature of 60�C. 7.2 If the pulp is in the form of wet sheets or rolls, dry the sample at a maximum temperature of 60�C. 7.3 Tear the sample into pieces of size approximately 5 �5 mm. If the pulp is difficult to defibre, split the sample by means of tweezers ( see Note ).
NOTE -- Dry disintegration, for example with a Wiley-mill, or wet disintegration, for example, with a high-speed stirrer, are not permitted.

7.4 Check that the pulp contains not more than 0.1 percent ash (see Note ). Before weighing, condition the sample for not less than 20 min in the atmosphere near the balance.
NOTE -- If the pulp to be tested contains more than 0.1 percent ash, determine the ash content of the alkali-insoluble fraction. Calculate the R-value on the basis of the ash-free pulp and the ash-free insoluble fraction.

8. PROCEDURE 8.1 Test Portion 8.1.1 Weigh, to the nearest 1 mg, about 2.5 g of the test sample. Then immediately weigh two separate test portions for the determination of the dry matter content in accordance with IS : 6213 (Part 21 )-1984*.
*Method of test for pulp: Part 21 Determination of dry matter content.

5

IS : 6213 ( Part 20 ) - 1984 8.2 Determination 8.2.1 Transfer the test portion to the beaker, add 25 ml of the sodium hydroxide solution adjusted to 20 � 0.2�C ( see Notes under 7.3 and 7.4 ), place the beaker in the constant temperature bath and allow the pulp to swell for 3 minutes. 8.2.2 Thoroughly defibre the pulp by stirring and macerating with the stirring rod for at least 3 min, macerating at a rate of 2 strokes per second. Add another 25 ml of the sodium hydroxide solutionat 20�C, stir until the suspension is uniform and dilute by adding 100 ml of the sodium hydroxide solution at 20�C. Cover the beaker with a watch-glass and leave in the constant temperature bath. 8.2.3 Sixty minutes after the first addition of the sodium hydroxide solution, stir the fibre suspension again and transfer it to the filtering device, fitted on a dry suction flask, adjusted to a temperature of 20 � 0.2�C in the constant temperature bath. 8.2.4 Apply suction only as long as the fibre mat is still covered with liquid in order that no air is sucked through the mat. Use the filtrate for rinsing the beaker and filter again through the slightly pressed fibre mat in order to collect all fibres. Finally, apply full suction briefly. The time for filtering and washing shall not exceed 20 min. 8.2.5 Compact the fibre mat, especially at the edges, cover with the acetic acid and allow 200 ml to pass through slowly without suction. Drain completely and wash with hot water until the filtrate is free from acid. 8.2.6 Cover the filtering device with the hand during the last washing in order that a vacuum is formed above the fibre mat. Then quickly release the vacuum in the suction flask in order to lift the fibre mat. Transfer the fibre mat, together with any remaining fibres adhering to the filtering device, by means of stainless steel tweezers, to the weighing bottle. 8.2.7 Place the open weighing bottle together with its lid in a drying oven and dry to constant mass at a temperature of 105 � 2�C (normally for 6 h). Allow the closed weighing bottle to cool in a desiccator and determine the mass of the alkali-insoluble fraction to the nearest 1 mg, after briefly raising the lid to allow equivalization of pressure. 8.2.8 Carry out at least two parallel determination on each test sample.
NOTE 1 -- In certain cases, for example, straw pulps, it is advisable to add initially only 15 or 20 ml of the sodium hydroxide solution to the pulp in order to facilitate defibering. The volume of alkali for the second addition has then to be increased to 35 or 30 ml respectively.

6

IS : 6213 ( Part 20 ) - 1984
NOTE 2 -- The solubility in 18 percent (m/m) sodium hydroxide solution is not affected by variations of a few degrees in temperature. At this concentration, the temperature may be kept at 20 � 2�C. TO solubility in sodium hydroxide solution of lower concentration [for example, 10 percent (m/m)] is much more dependent on temperature, At this lower concentration, the temperature should be kept at 20�0.2�C.

9. EXPRESSION OF RESULTS 9.1 Method of Calculation and Formula -- The alkali resistance, Rc, expressed as a percentage by mass, is given by the formula:

where m0 = the mass, in grams, of the test portion calculated on an oven-dry basis; and m1 = the oven-dry mass, in grams, of the alkali-insoluble fraction. 9.2 Precision and Expression of Results 9.2.1 The results of the parallel determinations should agree to within 0.3 percent. 9.2.2 Report the mean alkali resistance to one decimal place, using the symbols R 18 , R 10 , etc.
NOTE-For pulps containing less than 0.1 percent ash and other non-carbohydrate materials, the value (100--Rc) approaches the value (S c ) determined by the method for alkali solubility of pulps.

10. TEST REPORT 10.1 The test report shall include the following particulars: a) The results and the method of expression used; b) Any unusual features noted during the determination; and c) Any operation not specified in this standard or regarded as optional, which may have affected the results.
